chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Rafa'ah who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who participated with another man regarding a slave girl of his, and said: 'If we profit from her, then half of the profit is for you, and if she is of little value (or incurs loss), then there is nothing upon you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not see any problem with this, if the master of the slave girl is pleased with it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on sharing profits and losses in a partnership with a slave?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) validates a specific profit-and-loss sharing arrangement in slave ownership, highlighting the principle of mutual consent (rida) as the cornerstone of contractual validity in Shia jurisprudence. It illustrates the flexibility of early Islamic commercial law, where risk allocation could be customized by agreement rather than fixed by rigid default rules, reflecting the practical economic realities of the time.
